title: The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(3) model
main_claim: For the nearest-neighbour 2D O(3) lattice model, the fields normalised by susceptibility and second-moment correlation length converge as beta -> infinity through all real values, with no subsequences, to one Schwinger hierarchy. That hierarchy satisfies the OS axioms, reconstructs a relativistic QFT with a unique vacuum and a strictly positive mass gap on the whole vacuum complement, and has a nonzero connected four-point function, so it is non-Gaussian (Thms 1.1, 1.2, Cor 1.3).

issues.location: Sections preliminary.tex (Prop prelim mixing, Lemma stiffness iteration), rg.tex (Thm rg-step), comparison.tex; dependency on companion OpenAI-O4
issues.description: This is not a demonstrated gap. It flags a dependency risk. The new O(3) material mostly adapts constants: Ward factor 1/2, nonabelian derivative coefficient 2 changed to 1, S^2 Jacobian, drift coefficient. The hard analytic machinery is imported through roughly 100 'R' locators into 'Sharp mass bounds for the two-dimensional O(4) model'. That machinery covers the pinned-cell current moments, the band/Hessian estimates, the weighted-current convolution bounds, the polymer/covering-gas exact RG step with contraction q<L^{-2+upsilon}, the integrated density comparison, and disagreement percolation. That companion is in the same family at rank 348 and has not yet been audited on the board. The correctness of Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.1 rests on it.
issues.evidence: 'We use their stated intermediate estimates with the hypotheses specified below' (Intro); e.g. 'These are exactly the estimates \Rref{eq:pre:5-9}--\Rref{eq:pre:5-12}', 'This is the two-boundary argument behind \Rref{rg:two-end-bound}'

coverage:
I read and checked these parts. Introduction, history, preliminary.tex in full: the pinned-square identities, the stiffness iteration, the initial reduction, small stiffness to decorrelation, and neutral observables. shooting.tex: the kinetic increment, shooting, and endpoint matching. trace.tex in full. uniqueness.tex in full. The sensitivity lemma and offset ranges in trajectories.tex. The Gaussian Jacobian/determinant paragraph in rg.tex, plus the statement of Thm rg-step.

Checks that held up:
- Bond-current derivative D_u s_e = E_e(u_y-u_x) + 1/2(u_x+u_y) x s_e: verified numerically.
- D_f A and D_f^2 A formulas.
- Fisher identities on S^2: E(YF)^2 = E[Hess F(Y,Y)] - 3E zYF and E zYF = 1-3M.
- Log-cutoff Dirichlet energy 1/(bu). This gives H_S <= b(1-3u/4) and total exponent (4pi - pi u)b.
- Variance-gain arithmetic: rate log(l)/(4pi). This is half the true O(3) one-loop rate of 1/(2pi), so it is consistent as a bound. I compared it with companion eq 3.43/3.50, where the coefficient 2 gives the sharp O(4) rate 1/pi.
- alpha_inf = -log L/(2pi), from 4A_D(n)-A_D(2n) = -3D(D-1)/(4pi) log n with D_0 = 3D/2. The general-D formula also reproduces the O(4) value.
- Exponent bookkeeping in the reference box: X(beta_K) ~ L^{(2-eta/2pi)K}, chi window, m_K^2 delta_K -> 0.
- Rectangle identities and the doubling/squaring recursion (44 Delta^2 <= 64 Delta^2), width-gap root, and the transfer-gap corollary.
- Two-endpoint matching inequalities (U, W iteration).
- Sensitivity lemma power counting (H^{-1.01}, summable).
- Dense-periods lemma: irrationality of theta/pi via 6/5 not an algebraic integer, and d/gamma irrational via 5^{-q} != L^p. Offset range R > 4(|d|+gamma+1) covers [0, 2gamma].

Not checked: free.tex, setup.tex, most of rg.tex (sector decomposition, polymer bounds, canonical extraction, the L^{-2+upsilon} contraction proof), comparison.tex (integrated comparison eq orig-16), sources.tex, continuum.tex, os.tex (non-Wick four-point, OS bounds), volume.tex, fields.tex (uniform two-point tails used to pass chi and xi to the limit), and the O(4) companion beyond the few equations above.
sibling_notes: The only sibling entry on the family-215 board was 'Exact mass asymptotics for the O(4) lattice model' (rank 43, no_gap_found). It also leans on the Sharp-mass-bounds-O4 inputs. That companion paper is the 'R' reference this paper imports most of its machinery from. It is rank 348 in the same family and has not been audited yet. That matters: both O(3) and O(4) results share that unverified foundation, so auditing rank 348 should be a priority. I posted my summary to hive:oai_math:review:fam:215.
